title: Majestic Defense
summary: Leave the tempting pawn alone: escort the advanced passer, imprison the king, and finish with a pawn mate.

nodes.question: Where should the king go after g4+?
nodes.explanation: Black has already accepted the rook sacrifice. Capturing the checking pawn is tempting, but the winning route supports the f2 pawn instead.

branches.title: Keep the pawn as a barrier and escort f2
commentary: Begin after ...Kxf5 and g4+. Black must answer the pawn check without losing the advanced f-pawn.
Kf4 is the only winning reply in the exact root. Black leaves g4 alone and heads for e3.
Kg2 approaches f2, trying to blockade and capture the advanced pawn.
Ke3 protects f2 directly and threatens ...Ke2, supporting promotion.
Kf1 blocks the promotion square. This selected defense leaves White’s king trapped in front of the pawn.
Kf3 protects e2 and g2. The king and f2 pawn now deny White’s king every legal step.
g5 is a waiting move. The pawn advances, but White’s king still cannot move.
e3 prepares ...e2 with check. Black’s king protects the square on which that pawn will land.
g6 is another selected waiting move. The remote knight on a8 cannot interrupt the immediate threat.
e2# checks f1 with the pawn. Kf3 protects e2 and g2; the f2 pawn controls e1 and g1, completing a king-and-pawn mate.
branches.explanation: e2# checks f1 with the pawn. Kf3 protects e2 and g2; the f2 pawn controls e1 and g1, completing a king-and-pawn mate.

branches.title: Capture the checking pawn
commentary: Compare the natural capture with the king’s purposeful central route.
Kxg4 removes the pawn but gives up the win. The king is too far away to protect f2 in time.
Kg2 reaches the blockade while the king cannot immediately escort f2. This exact knight-and-pawn position is drawn with best play.
branches.explanation: Kg2 reaches the blockade while the king cannot immediately escort f2. This exact knight-and-pawn position is drawn with best play.

branches.title: Retreat from the checking pawn
commentary: A retreat also answers the check, but does not improve the passer’s support.
Ke5 abandons the winning route to e3. The tablebase evaluates the position as drawn.
Kg2 uses the lost tempo to approach f2. This independently selected reply illustrates the same blockade resource.

exercises.prompt: Why is the g4 pawn more useful alive?
exercises.answer: Taking it sends Black’s king away from the passer. Kf4 instead reaches e3 in time to defend f2 before White can remove it.

exercises.prompt: Why can a pawn deliver mate without promoting?
exercises.answer: The king on f3 protects e2 and g2, while the f2 pawn takes e1 and g1. Advancing the e-pawn to e2 checks the trapped king on f1.

startContext: Begin after White’s rook sacrifice has been accepted and g4+ is on the board, at 123 seconds. Earlier rook checks and the sacrifice remain source context. The selected king escort and two drawing deviations are checked here.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
